summary: This article explains how dolphins breathe air, raise their calves, hunt as a team, find food with echoes, call each other by whistles, sleep with half the brain, and why they need a clean sea.
introduce: Show the title “Dolphins: Smart Swimmers” and give pairs one minute to predict, in one sentence, what the whole article is mostly about. Write three predictions on the board and tell students they will check which one is closest to the main idea after reading.

keyTerms.def: an animal that breathes air and feeds its babies milk
the top part or outside layer of something
a group of dolphins or whales that live and travel together

challengeTerms.def: to work together with others toward the same goal
one of the two halves of the brain (or of a sphere such as Earth)
animals that are caught by accident in nets meant for other kinds of fish

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that dolphins are smarter than most other sea animals? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how dolphins use sound to survive.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review mammal, surface, and pod, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use cooperate, hemisphere, and bycatch in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
